1.1: This Paul talkin'—a servant of Christ Jesus. God called me to be an apostle and set me apart to spread His good news.
1.2: This the same good news God promised a long time ago through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures.
1.3: It's all about His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, who came from David's bloodline in the flesh—
1.4: but was shown to be God's Son with real power, through the Holy Spirit, when He rose up from the dead.
1.5: Through Jesus, we got grace and this calling to go tell all nations 'bout obeyin' the faith for His name's sake.
1.6: And y'all? Y'all part of that too—called out by Jesus Christ.
1.7: To everybody out there in Rome, who God loves and called to be holy: Grace and peace to y'all from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.8: First off, lemme say—I thank my God through Jesus for all y'all. Word about y'all's faith done spread across the whole world.
1.9: God knows I ain't lyin'. I serve Him with my spirit in spreadin' this gospel 'bout His Son, and I always lift y'all up in prayer.
1.10: I been prayin', askin' if maybe now, finally, God'll make a way for me to come see y'all.
1.11: I really wanna be with you—so I can give y'all some spiritual gift, help y'all stay grounded and strong.
1.12: But not just that—I wanna be encouraged too, by our faith mixin' together, mine and yours.
1.13: I want y'all to know—I been tryna come to y'all, plenty times. But somethin' always came up. I was tryna get some spiritual fruit among y'all like I did with the other Gentiles.
1.14: I owe it to everybody—Greeks, non-Greeks, the educated and the ones who ain't.
1.15: So I'm all the way ready to preach the gospel to y'all in Rome too.
1.16: I ain't ashamed of the gospel, nah—not at all. That's God's power right there to save anybody who believes. First for the Jews, then the Gentiles.
1.17: 'Cause in this gospel, God's righteousness gets revealed—startin' in faith, and leadin' to more faith. Like Scripture says: "The ones who right with God gon' live by faith."
1.18: God's wrath straight up comin' down from heaven on all the folks out here livin' foul, hidin' the truth with wickedness.
1.19: They already got some knowledge of God—He made it plain to 'em.
1.20: Ever since the world been created, God's invisible stuff—His power, His divinity—it's been loud and clear through what He made. So they got no excuse.
1.21: Even though they knew God, they ain't give Him glory or thanks. Instead, they got caught up in foolish thinkin', and their hearts went dark.
1.22: They thought they was smart—but they played theyself.
1.23: They traded God's unshakable glory for man-made idols—images of humans, birds, animals, and snakes.
1.24: So God said, "Bet." He let 'em go head and follow them dirty desires, messin' up their own bodies with each other.
1.25: They switched God's truth for lies, and started worshipin' created things instead of the Creator—who deserves all the praise forever. Amen.
1.26: That's why God let 'em chase after shameful lusts. Women started sleepin' with each other instead of men,
1.27: and the men, same thing—burnin' with lust for other men, doin' shameful stuff. And they dealt with the consequences that came with it.
1.28: Since they ain't wanna keep God in their minds, He let 'em go—gave 'em over to a twisted mindset, and they started livin' wild.
1.29: They was full of all kinds of wrong—sexual sin, evil, greed, hate. Envy, murder, beef, deceit, messiness.
1.30: Gossipers, backstabbers, God-haters. Arrogant, prideful, loud with the sin. Creators of evil, disobedient to parents,
1.32: And even though they know what God says—that folks who do this deserve judgment—they still do it… and cheer on the ones who do too.

2.1: So look—you got no excuse, whoever you are, tryna judge other folks. 'Cause when you point fingers, you really callin' yourself out—you doin' the same stuff.
2.2: And we know God's judgment is real and rooted in truth. He gon' judge folks who live like that.
2.3: You think just 'cause you judge other folks, but still doin' what they do, that you gon' skip God's judgment? You wild.
2.4: Or do you disrespect the goodness, patience, and mercy of God—forgettin' that His kindness is supposed to lead you to repentance?
2.5: But if your heart hard and you keep ignorin' Him, all you doin' is stackin' up wrath for yourself when God finally reveals His righteous judgment.
2.6: 'Cause He gon' repay everybody based on what they do—
2.7: Folks who stay consistent, keep doin' good, and lookin' for glory, honor, and eternal life? They gon' get eternal life.
2.8: But folks out for self, rejectin' truth, and ridin' with wickedness? God got wrath and judgment lined up.
2.9: Trouble and stress for every soul that keeps doin' evil—Jew first, then everybody else.
2.10: But glory, honor, and peace to everybody who does good—again, Jew first, then the rest.
2.12: People who sin without knowin' the law? They still gon' be judged outside the law. And folks who sin while knowin' the law? They gon' be judged by it.
2.13: 'Cause it ain't the folks who hear the law that are right in God's eyes—it's the ones who do it that get justified.
2.14: Even when Gentiles, who ain't got the written law, follow it naturally—they show that they got the law in them.
2.15: They show that it's written on their hearts. Their conscience speaks, their thoughts go back and forth—sometimes accusin', sometimes defendin'.
2.16: And on that day, God gon' judge all the hidden stuff folks keep tucked inside—through Jesus Christ, just like my gospel says.
2.17: Now look—if you call yourself a Jew, relyin' on the law, braggin' on God,
2.18: Knowin' His will, and cosignin' the good stuff 'cause you been taught the law,
2.19: And you so sure you a guide for the blind, a light for folks in the dark,
2.20: A teacher for the immature, someone with the full scoop on truth and knowledge from the law—
2.21: Then let me ask you: you teachin' others, but do you teach yourself? You say don't steal—do you steal?
2.22: You say don't cheat—do you cheat? You hate idols—do you rob temples?
2.23: You brag on the law—but when you break it, you makin' God look bad.
2.24: 'Cause it's written: "God's name gets disrespected among the Gentiles 'cause of y'all." That's on y'all.
2.25: Bein' circumcised only helps if you actually keep the law. But if you break it, then your circumcision don't mean nothin'.
2.26: So if a man who ain't circumcised follows God's law, ain't that just as good as bein' circumcised?
2.27: And if he ain't got the physical sign, but lives right, he'll end up judgin' you—you who got the written law and circumcision, but still break it.
2.28: Bein' a Jew ain't just about lookin' the part on the outside.
2.29: A real Jew is one on the inside. And real circumcision? It's not about the flesh—it's in the heart, done by the Spirit, not the letter. And that kinda person don't need applause from people—they get praise straight from God.

3.1: So what's the point of bein' Jewish then? Or what's the gain from gettin' circumcised?
3.2: Plenty! First off—God trusted them with His Word. That's big.
3.3: Now, what if some of them ain't believe? That don't cancel out God's faithfulness, does it?
3.4: Nah! Not at all. Let God be real, even if every human turn out to be a liar. Like Scripture say: "You right when You speak, Lord, And You still stand strong when folks come at You."
3.5: But hold up—if our wrongness just makes God's righteousness look even better, what we sayin'? Is God wrong for bringin' judgment? (I'm speakin' how folks do.)
3.6: Absolutely not! 'Cause how could God judge the whole world if He was unfair?
3.7: And if my lie made God's truth shine even more, why I still gotta be judged like I'm wrong?
3.8: Some folks even twisted what we said like this: "Well then, let's do bad so good can come from it." If that's how they movin', they deserve that judgment. Period.
3.9: So what now? Are we better than them? Nope. Not at all. We already said—Jews and Gentiles alike—we all caught up in sin.
3.10: Like the Scriptures say: "Ain't nobody righteous. Not even one.
3.11: Ain't nobody really understands or chasin' after God.
3.12: Everybody done veered off the path. Ain't nobody doin' right—not a single one."
3.13: "Their throat like an open grave. They slick with the tongue—always lyin'. Venom under their lips,
3.14: Mouth full of curses and bitterness."
3.16: Wherever they go, pain and destruction follow.
3.17: They don't know nothin' about peace.
3.18: And they walk like they don't even see God."
3.19: We know that the law talkin' to the folks who under it—so everybody's mouth gets shut, and the whole world stand guilty before God.
3.20: 'Cause tryin' to be good by the law? That won't justify nobody. The law just shows us how messed up we really are.
3.21: But now—God's righteousness done been revealed outside the law. And the Law and Prophets been talkin' 'bout it all along.
3.22: This righteousness comes through faith in Jesus Christ, and it's for everybody who believes. No difference—
3.23: 'Cause all have sinned and fell short of God's glory.
3.24: But we get made right with God freely, by His grace, through what Jesus did to redeem us.
3.25: God put Jesus out there as a sacrifice, a blood offering to cover us—only accessed through faith. That way, God shows He's righteous, even though He let some sins slide in the past.
3.26: He did it to prove right now that He's both just and the one who makes people righteous—if they got faith in Jesus.
3.27: So where's the braggin' rights? Gone. By what rule? Tryin' to earn it? Nope—it's by faith.
3.28: So here's what we know: folks get right with God by faith, not by tryna check off rules.
3.29: Or is God just for Jews? Nah. He's for the Gentiles too.
3.30: 'Cause there's only one God, and He gon' make both the circumcised and uncircumcised right with Him—through faith.
3.31: So we throw out the law just 'cause we got faith now? Nah, fam—we actually uphold it by understandin' what it was pointin' to all along.

4.1: So what we sayin' about Abraham, our forefather? What did he gain from all this by doin' it in his own strength?
4.2: 'Cause if Abraham got made right by his own works, he'd have a reason to brag—but not in front of God.
4.3: What do the Scriptures say? "Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness."
4.4: Now if you work for it, what you get ain't a gift—it's what you earned. That's a paycheck, not grace.
4.5: But if you ain't workin', yet you trust the One who makes sinners right? That faith is counted as righteousness.
4.6: That's what David was talkin' 'bout when he said how blessed the person is that God makes right without keepin' all the rules:
4.7: "Blessed is the one whose mess-ups are forgiven, whose sins are covered.
4.8: Blessed is the one the Lord don't hold sin against."
4.9: So this blessing David talked about—is it just for folks who circumcised? Or does it apply to the uncircumcised too? Remember: Abraham's faith was credited to him as righteousness.
4.10: But when did that happen? Was it after he got circumcised or before? It was before.
4.11: He got circumcised later as a sign, like a receipt of the righteousness he already had through faith. That way, he became the father of all who believe—even if they not circumcised—so they could be made right too.
4.12: And he's also the father of the ones who are circumcised—but not just by flesh, they walkin' in the same kind of faith he had before all that.
4.13: The promise that Abraham would inherit the world ain't come through the law—it came through the righteousness of faith.
4.14: 'Cause if folks who follow the law are the only ones who get the promise, then faith don't mean nothin' and the promise is canceled.
4.15: The law brings wrath, period. And if there ain't no law, then folks don't even know they sinnin'.
4.16: That's why it's all about faith—so the promise rests on grace. That way, it's guaranteed for all Abraham's people—not just the law-keepers, but everybody who shares his faith.
4.17: Like God said, "I made you the father of many nations." And Abraham believed God—the One who gives life to the dead and speaks things into existence like they already there.
4.18: Even when hope looked dead, Abraham kept hopin' and believed. And just like God said, "Your descendants gon' be like this"—it came to pass.
4.19: Abraham ain't trip over how old he was (almost 100), or how dead Sarah's womb looked. His faith ain't fold.
4.20: He ain't waver on God's promise. He got stronger in his faith and gave God glory.
4.21: He was fully convinced that God could do exactly what He promised.
4.22: And because of that, it was credited to him as righteousness.
4.23: And that ain't just about Abraham—it was written for us too.
4.24: We get that same credit if we believe in the One who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
4.25: Jesus was handed over 'cause of our sins, and He was raised so we could be made right with God.

5.1: Since we been made right with God through faith, we got peace with Him now—through our Lord Jesus Christ.
5.2: And it's through Jesus we get access to this grace we stand in right now. So we celebrate, hopin' for the glory God gon' reveal.
5.3: But we don't just celebrate when things good—we even give God glory in our struggles, 'cause we know trouble builds perseverance,
5.4: perseverance builds character, and character leads to real hope.
5.5: And that hope don't play us—it don't disappoint. 'Cause God's love done been poured deep into our hearts through the Holy Spirit He gave us.
5.6: When we was still weak—strugglin', stuck, and had nothin' to offer—Christ died for us, the ungodly. Right on time.
5.7: Like, barely anybody would die for a righteous person. Maybe for a good one, somebody might risk it…
5.8: But God showed love on a whole different level: while we was still sinners, Christ died for us.
5.9: And now that we been made right by His blood, best believe we gon' be saved from God's judgment too.
5.10: If He made things right when we was enemies through His death, then now that we good with Him? We gon' be saved through His life.
5.11: And not just that—we celebrate God now, 'cause through Jesus, we got reconciliation locked in.
5.12: Just like sin entered the world through one man, and death showed up through that sin—now death be spreadin' to everybody, 'cause everybody sinned.
5.13: Even before the law came, sin was in the world. But when there ain't no law, it ain't held against you the same way.
5.14: Still, death ruled from Adam all the way to Moses—even over folks who ain't sin the exact way Adam did. Adam was a preview—a prototype—for the One who was comin'.
5.15: But the gift ain't like the fall. 'Cause if many died 'cause of one man's mess-up, then way more people gon' live because of God's grace and that gift that came through Jesus.
5.16: And the gift ain't like what came from Adam's mistake. His one sin brought condemnation—but this gift? It covers many sins and brings justification.
5.17: If death ran the show 'cause of one man's fall, how much more gon' those who get grace and righteousness rule in life through Jesus?
5.18: So just like one man's offense brought guilt on everybody, one Man's righteous act brought life and justification to everybody.
5.19: One man's disobedience made us all sinners—but one Man's obedience? That's makin' a whole lotta folks righteous.
5.20: The law came in so we'd see just how deep sin goes. But where sin tried to overflow—grace overflowed even more.
5.21: So just like sin used to run the show and lead to death, now grace run things—lead to righteousness, and that righteousness leads to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

6.1: So what we sayin'? Should we keep sinnin' just so grace can keep showin' up?
6.2: Absolutely not! If we dead to sin, how we gon' keep livin' in it like nothin' changed?
6.3: Don't y'all know—when we got baptized into Christ Jesus, we was baptized into His death?
6.4: That means we were buried with Him through baptism. And just like Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too should be walkin' in a whole new life.
6.5: If we united with Him in His death, best believe we gon' be united with Him in His resurrection too.
6.6: Know this—our old self got nailed to the cross with Him, so sin wouldn't run our lives no more. We ain't slaves to it now.
6.7: 'Cause when you dead, you free from sin's grip.
6.8: And if we died with Christ, we believe we gon' live with Him too.
6.9: We know Jesus got up from the dead, and He ain't ever dyin' again. Death can't touch Him no more.
6.10: He died once—and that death took care of sin. But now? He livin' fully for God.
6.11: Same with y'all—consider yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God through Christ Jesus our Lord.
6.12: So don't let sin act like it own your body. Don't obey its cravings.
6.13: Don't use your body parts for wickedness. Instead, give yourself fully to God—like somebody who came back from the dead. Let your whole self be an instrument for righteousness.
6.14: Sin ain't got no power over you anymore. You ain't under law—you under grace.
6.15: So what now? Since we not under law but under grace, we should go ahead and sin? Nah.
6.16: Don't you know whoever you obey—you a slave to that? Either you obey sin and end up in death, or you obey God and walk in righteousness.
6.17: But thank God—y'all used to be slaves to sin, but now you obeyin' from the heart the teaching that saved you.
6.18: And since you've been set free from sin, now you livin' right—servants of righteousness.
6.19: I'm breakin' it down plain 'cause we all got limits. Just like you used to use your body for mess—doin' dirt on dirt—now use your body for righteousness, leading you into a holy life.
6.20: When you was locked in sin, you ain't care about righteousness.
6.21: But what did that really get you? Just shame. And where'd it lead? Death.
6.22: But now you free from all that—God got you. And now your life bearin' fruit that's holy, and the end of it all? Eternal life.
6.23: 'Cause the paycheck sin pays out is death. But the gift God gives? That's eternal life—through Christ Jesus our Lord.

7.1: Y'all know how the law work, right? (I'm talkin' to folks who know the law.) The law only got authority over somebody while they still alive.
7.2: Like a married woman—she bound by law to her husband while he alive. But if he dies, she free from that law.
7.3: If she marry somebody else while he still alive, that's adultery. But if he's dead, she free. She ain't no adulterer if she remarry.
7.4: Same way, fam—through Jesus' body, we died to the law so we could be joined to somebody new: the risen Christ. Now we supposed to bear fruit for God.
7.5: Back when we was caught up in the flesh, our sinful cravings (which the law actually stirred up) had us actin' out—and all that mess was leadin' to death.
7.6: But now we free. We done died to what had us locked up. Now we servin' in a new way—through the Spirit, not by the old letter of the law.
7.7: So what we sayin'? The law sinful now? No way. I wouldn't even know what sin was if the law ain't tell me. Like, I wouldn't know it was wrong to be greedy if the law ain't said, "Don't covet."
7.8: But sin used the command to stir up all kinds of wrong desires in me. Without the law, sin ain't got power like that.
7.9: I used to think I was alive without the law. But when I really saw the command, sin rose up and I died inside.
7.10: The command that was supposed to bring life? It showed me how deep in death I was.
7.11: Sin tricked me, used the law like a trap, and killed me with it.
7.12: But listen—the law itself? It's holy. The command is holy. Just and good.
7.13: So did somethin' good turn into death for me? Nah. It was sin—showin' just how sinful it really is. It used what's good to bring me death, so I'd really see how wild sin gets when exposed by the law.
7.14: The law spiritual—but me? I'm flesh. Sold out to sin like a slave.
7.15: I don't even understand myself sometimes. The stuff I wanna do, I don't do. But the stuff I hate? That's what I end up doin'.
7.16: So when I do what I don't wanna do, I'm really agreein' the law is good.
7.17: But now, it ain't even really me—it's the sin livin' in me.
7.18: I know in me (in my flesh), nothin' good lives. I wanna do right, but I don't got the strength to carry it out.
7.19: The good I wanna do? I don't. The evil I'm tryin' to avoid? That's what I keep doin'.
7.20: So if I'm doin' what I don't wanna do—it ain't just me, it's that sin still residin' in me.
7.21: So here's what I found: even when I wanna do right, evil still lurkin'.
7.22: Deep down, I love God's law—
7.23: but I see this other law in me, fightin' against my mind. It's tryna trap me back into sin's control.
7.24: I'm torn up inside. Who gon' save me from this body that's draggin' me toward death?
7.25: Thank God—Jesus Christ our Lord did that! So now, with my mind, I serve God's law. But in this flesh, sin still tryin' to call shots.

8.1: So now there ain't no condemnation for the ones who in Christ Jesus—folks who ain't walkin' in the flesh, but movin' in the Spirit.
8.2: 'Cause the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus done set me free from the law of sin and death.
8.3: The law couldn't save us—it was too weak 'cause of our flesh. But God stepped in—He sent His own Son, lookin' just like us, to deal with sin. And He shut sin down in the flesh.
8.4: So now the righteous standard of the law gets fulfilled in us—the ones who walk by the Spirit, not by the flesh.
8.5: Folks who live for the flesh? They mind stay on fleshly things. But folks who live by the Spirit? They mind stay on Spirit stuff.
8.6: A fleshly mind leads to death. But a Spirit-filled mind brings life and peace.
8.7: That fleshly mind fights God—don't follow God's law, and it can't.
8.8: So people still caught in the flesh can't please God.
8.9: But that ain't you—if God's Spirit live in you. And if you don't have the Spirit of Christ, you ain't really His.
8.10: If Christ is in you, yeah, your body dead because of sin—but your spirit is alive 'cause of righteousness.
8.11: And if the same Spirit that raised Jesus from the dead lives in you? Then that Spirit gon' bring your mortal body to life too. That's real.
8.12: So fam, we don't owe nothin' to the flesh—we ain't gotta live like that no more.
8.13: If you live by the flesh, you gon' die. But if you let the Spirit kill off those body-born cravings, you gon' live.
8.14: The ones led by God's Spirit? Those are God's children.
8.15: You ain't receive no spirit of fear or bondage—you got the Spirit of adoption. That's why we cry out, "Abba! Father!"
8.16: The Holy Spirit backs it up—our spirit and His agree: we God's kids.
8.17: And if we His kids, then we His heirs—joint-heirs with Christ. That means we gon' suffer with Him, but we also gon' be glorified with Him.
8.18: I'm convinced: the pain we dealin' with now don't even compare to the glory that's comin'.
8.19: Creation itself is out here waitin' on the children of God to be revealed.
8.20: 'Cause creation got put into frustration—not by choice, but by the One who allowed it—with hope still in place.
8.21: 'Cause even creation gon' be set free from its decay and step into the freedom God's kids already got.
8.22: The whole world been groanin' like it's in labor—up until now.
8.23: And we groanin' too—us who got the Spirit's first fruits. We waitin' for full adoption, for our bodies to be redeemed.
8.24: We were saved in this hope—but if you already see it, it ain't hope. Who hopes for what they already got?
8.25: But if we hopin' for what we can't see, we wait for it with patience.
8.26: The Spirit helps us in our weakness—when we don't even know what to pray for, the Spirit steps in, intercedin' with deep groans words can't express.
8.27: And God, who knows hearts, understands what the Spirit's sayin', 'cause He prays for the saints right in line with God's will.
8.28: And we know everything workin' together for good—for those who love God and are called for His purpose.
8.29: The ones God knew ahead of time, He also destined to be shaped like His Son—so Jesus could be the firstborn of many siblings.
8.30: And the ones He destined, He also called. The ones He called, He justified. And the ones He justified? He glorified.
8.31: So what we gon' say about all this? If God be for us, who can be against us?
8.32: He ain't even spare His own Son—but gave Him up for all of us. So won't He give us everything else too?
8.33: Who gon' accuse God's chosen? God's the one who justifies.
8.34: Who tryna condemn us? Christ died—and more than that, He rose! Now He sittin' at the right hand of God, still intercedin' for us.
8.35: What gon' separate us from Christ's love? Trouble? Pain? Hatred? Hunger? Homelessness? Danger? Violence?
8.36: Like Scripture said: "We gettin' killed all day long—for You. We look like sheep sent to the slaughter."
8.37: But even with all that—we more than conquerors through the One who loved us.
8.38: I'm fully convinced—death or life, angels or demons, present or future, powers,
8.39: height or depth—nothin, not even created stuff, can separate us from God's love that's in Christ Jesus our Lord.

9.1: I'm tellin' the truth in Christ—I ain't lyin'. My own conscience, guided by the Holy Spirit, backs me up.
9.2: My heart heavy with pain. I'm grievin' non-stop.
9.3: I'd even take the curse on myself—be cut off from Christ—if it meant savin' my own people, my family in the flesh.
9.4: They Israelites. They had the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the law, the temple service, the promises—
9.5: the patriarchs came from them, and straight up, Jesus came through their line too—who is over everything, God forever blessed. Amen.
9.6: But don't get it twisted—God's word ain't failed. Just 'cause someone from Israel don't mean they truly Israel.
9.7: And not everybody who came from Abraham's bloodline is counted as his children. Scripture said, "In Isaac your seed shall be called."
9.8: That mean the flesh-born kids ain't automatically God's kids. The ones born by promise—they the real seed.
9.9: The promise went like this: "At this time next year, I'ma come through and Sarah gon' have a son."
9.10: And check this—Rebekah had twins by one man, Isaac, our father.
9.11: Before they were even born—before they did anything good or bad—God already had purpose. Not based on works, but on the One who calls.
9.12: He told her straight: "The older gon' serve the younger."
9.13: Just like Scripture say: "Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated."
9.14: So what we sayin'? God unjust? No way.
9.15: He told Moses, "I'll show mercy to whoever I choose, and compassion to whoever I want."
9.16: So it ain't about who wants it or works for it—it's about God showin' mercy.
9.17: Look at Pharaoh—Scripture says, "I raised you up so I could flex My power through you and let the whole world know My name."
9.18: So God shows mercy to who He wants—and He hardens hearts when He wants too.
9.19: So then you might ask, "How God still blame folks? Ain't nobody resistin' His will."
9.20: But hold up—who are you to talk back to God? Can what's made talk to the Maker and say, "Why you make me like this?"
9.21: Don't the potter got authority over the clay—to make one pot for honor and another for trash?
9.22: What if God, wantin' to show His wrath and power, put up with folks made for destruction—patiently—
9.23: just so He could show off the riches of His glory to the ones He made for mercy?
9.24: And that's us—not just Jews, but Gentiles too.
9.25: Like He said in Hosea: "I'ma call folks My people who ain't even My people. I'ma call her loved who wasn't loved."
9.26: And, "In the same place they was told, 'Y'all not My people,' they gon' be called sons of the livin' God."
9.27: And Isaiah shouted this about Israel: "Even if Israel's people was as many as sand on the beach, only a remnant gon' be saved."
9.28: "The Lord gon' finish what He started. He gon' wrap it up quick and in righteousness."
9.29: And just like Isaiah said before: "If the Lord of Hosts hadn't left us some folks, we'd be like Sodom and Gomorrah—straight wiped out."
9.30: So what's the takeaway? The Gentiles, who wasn't even chasin' righteousness, got it—because they came through faith.
9.31: But Israel, who been chasin' righteousness through the law, ain't catch it.
9.32: Why? 'Cause they was tryin' to earn it through works—not through faith. And they tripped over the stumbling block.
9.33: Like it's written: "Look, I'm layin' down a stone in Zion—a stone folks gon' trip on. But whoever believes in Him won't be ashamed."

10.1: Family, my heart's desire and my prayer to God for Israel is that they get saved.
10.2: I can testify—they got a real zeal for God, but it ain't grounded in truth.
10.3: They tryna make their own righteousness work, instead of submitting to the righteousness that comes from God.
10.4: But Christ? He the end of all that law-based righteousness—for everybody who believes.
10.5: Moses said, "The one who lives by the law gotta keep every part of it."
10.6: But the righteousness that comes from faith don't talk like that. It don't say, "Who gon' go up to heaven?" (like you gotta bring Christ down),
10.7: or "Who gon' go down to the grave?" (like you gotta raise Christ up).
10.8: What it does say is: "The word is right here—near you. It's in your mouth and in your heart." That's the word of faith we been preachin'.
10.9: So if you say with your mouth, "Jesus is Lord," and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead—you will be saved.
10.10: 'Cause with your heart you believe and get made right, and with your mouth you confess and receive salvation.
10.11: Scripture say, "Whoever believes in Him won't be put to shame."
10.12: It don't matter if you Jew or Greek—same Lord over everybody, and He got blessings for all who call on Him.
10.13: "Whoever calls on the name of the Lord gon' be saved." Period.
10.14: But how they gon' call on someone they ain't believe in? And how they gon' believe if they ain't never heard about Him? And how they gon' hear without somebody preachin'?
10.15: And how folks gon' preach unless they been sent? Like the Word says:"How beautiful are the feet of them who bring good news—who preach peace and bring glad tidings of good things."
10.16: But everybody ain't listen to the gospel. Isaiah said, "Lord, who believed what we said?"
10.17: So faith comes from hearin'—and hearin' comes from the Word of Christ.
10.18: But hold up—did they really not hear? Oh they heard:"Their voice went out to the whole earth,Their words to the ends of the world."
10.19: Did Israel really not understand? First Moses said:"I'ma make y'all jealous with a nation that ain't even a nation. I'ma provoke you with some folks who don't even look the part."
10.20: Then Isaiah got bold and said:"I let folks find Me who wasn't even lookin'. I made Myself known to people who ain't even ask for Me."
10.21: But about Israel? God said,"All day long I held out My hands to a hard-headed, rebellious people."

11.1: So let me ask—has God tossed His people out? No way! I'm an Israelite myself—from Abraham's bloodline, from the tribe of Benjamin.
11.2: God ain't abandoned His people who He knew from the jump. Don't you remember what Scripture say 'bout Elijah? He was complainin' to God about Israel:
11.3: "Lord, they killed Your prophets, tore down Your altars, and I'm the only one left. Now they tryna kill me too."
11.4: But God told him, "Nah—I got 7,000 on reserve who ain't bowed to Baal."
11.5: Same thing now—God got a remnant, chosen by grace.
11.6: And if it's by grace, it ain't about works. Otherwise, grace wouldn't even be grace anymore.
11.7: So what's the deal? Israel didn't get what it was lookin' for. But the chosen did. The rest got hardened.
11.8: Just like it's written: "God gave 'em spiritual dullness—Eyes that couldn't see, Ears that couldn't hear—And they still like that to this day."
11.9: And David said: "Let their table trap 'em, Let it be a snare and a payback.
11.10: Let their eyes go blind, And their backs stay bent."
11.11: So again—did they stumble just to fall flat forever? Nope! Their fall opened the door for the Gentiles, to make 'em jealous.
11.12: If their fall brought riches to the world, imagine what their comeback gon' bring. That gon' hit different.
11.13: Now I'm talkin' to my Gentile folks—this is my ministry, and I'm proud of it.
11.14: I'm tryna make my own people jealous so maybe some of them will be saved.
11.15: 'Cause if their rejection brought reconciliation to the world, their acceptance gon' be like life from the dead.
11.16: If the first part of the dough holy, the whole batch holy. If the root's holy, so are the branches.
11.17: Now, some branches got cut off, and you—a wild olive shoot—got grafted in. You now share in that holy root.
11.18: Don't be braggin' like you better than the original branches. Remember—you ain't holdin' the root up. The root holdin' you.
11.19: You might say, "They got cut so I could get in."
11.20: Okay, but they got cut 'cause they ain't believe. And you stand 'cause of faith. So stay humble, not arrogant.
11.21: If God ain't spare the original branches, don't think He won't check you too.
11.22: So take in both sides of God—His kindness and His severity. He was hard on those who fell, but He's been kind to you—as long as you stay in that kindness. Otherwise? You could get cut off too.
11.23: But if they stop their unbelief, God can graft them back in just like that.
11.24: 'Cause if He could graft you—a wild branch—into His tree, how much easier is it to bring the original branches back?
11.25: Look, I don't want y'all to miss this mystery and get full of yourselves—Israel got a partial blindness for now, but it ain't forever. Once the Gentiles come in full…
11.26: All Israel gon' be saved. Like Scripture say: "The Deliverer gon' come from Zion And turn Jacob from all his mess.
11.27: This my promise to them—I'm takin' their sins away."
11.28: Right now, they enemies 'cause of the gospel—for your sake. But when it comes to God's choosing? They still loved because of the forefathers.
11.29: God's gifts and His call ain't never gettin' revoked.
11.30: Just like y'all were once disobedient and now got mercy 'cause they disobeyed,
11.31: Now they disobedient so they can receive mercy through your mercy.
11.32: God allowed everybody to fall short so He could show everybody mercy.
11.33: Ohhh the depths of God's riches, wisdom, and knowledge! His judgments too deep to trace. His ways can't be mapped out.
11.34: "Who really knows God's mind? Who gave Him advice?"
11.35: "Who gave God anything first that He owe them back?"
11.36: Everything came from Him, flows through Him, and exists for Him. To Him be all glory, forever. Amen.

12.1: So look, fam—I'm beggin' you, by God's mercy, give your whole self to Him. Let your body be a living sacrifice—holy and pleasing to God. That's the least you can do.
12.2: Don't let the world squeeze you into its mold. Be transformed—from the inside out—by renewin' your mind. Then you'll know what God really wants: what's good, what's pleasing, and what's perfect.
12.3: By the grace God gave me, I'm tellin' each of y'all—don't think you more than you are. Stay humble. Think real about yourself, based on the faith God gave you.
12.4: Just like a body got many parts, and all the parts do different things—
12.5: same way, we all one body in Christ. And each of us belong to each other. We in this together.
12.6: We all got different gifts, 'cause God gave us different kinds of grace. So use 'em!
12.7: If your gift is servin', then serve. If it's teachin', teach.
12.8: If it's encouragement, encourage. If it's givin', give with no stinginess. If you lead, do it with hustle. If you show mercy, do it with joy.
12.9: Love ain't supposed to be fake. Hate what's evil, hold on tight to what's good.
12.10: Show real love for one another like fam. Be quick to honor others over yourself.
12.11: Don't be lazy—stay lit in the Spirit, servin' the Lord.
12.12: Be joyful when you hope, patient when you hurt, faithful when you pray.
12.13: Share what you got with God's people in need. Always be ready to open your door.
12.14: Bless the folks who come at you—don't curse 'em, bless 'em.
12.15: Celebrate with those who celebratin', cry with those who cryin'.
12.16: Be in sync with each other. Don't act all high and mighty—vibe with the humble. Don't think you the smartest in the room.
12.17: Don't pay evil back with evil. Try to do what's right in front of everybody.
12.18: If it's possible, and it's up to you—live in peace with folks.
12.19: Don't go takin' revenge, fam. Let God handle that. Like Scripture says, "Vengeance is Mine—I'll pay it back," says the Lord.
12.20: Instead: If your enemy hungry, feed 'em. If they thirsty, give 'em something to drink. That'll heat coals on their head—and maybe their heart too.
12.21: Don't let evil beat you. Flip it—overcome evil with good.

13.1: Everybody need to fall in line under the folks in power—'cause ain't no authority unless God allowed it. And the ones that exist? God put 'em in place.
13.2: So if you fight the system, you really fightin' what God set up. And if you do that, judgment comin'.
13.3: Folks in charge ain't supposed to scare people doin' right—they supposed to check folks doin' wrong. You wanna stay outta trouble? Then do right, and they'll respect you.
13.4: 'Cause the one in authority workin' for God to help keep things good. But if you wildin'? You better be scared. That power ain't for show. They carryin' it to deal with evil.
13.5: So yeah, obey—'cause you don't wanna get punished, and so your conscience stay clean.
13.6: That's why you pay taxes too—these folks in office? They full-time in that role, actin' as God's servants.
13.7: So give what's owed: taxes to who you owe taxes, fees to who you owe fees, respect to who's due respect, and honor to who's due honor.
13.8: Don't owe nobody nothin'—except love. That's a debt you always pay. 'Cause if you love your neighbor, you already fulfillin' the law.
13.9: All them commandments—"Don't cheat, don't kill, don't steal, don't lie, don't be greedy"—they all get wrapped up in one line: "Love your neighbor like you love yourself."
13.10: Love don't hurt your neighbor. That's why love is the full expression of the law.
13.11: And on top of all that, know what time it is—it's time to wake up. Salvation's closer now than when we first believed.
13.12: The night almost over. The day about to break. So we need to throw off that darkness and gear up with the armor of light.
13.13: Let's move right—like we out in the daylight. No wild partyin', no drunk nights, no freaky business, no jealousy and drama.
13.14: Instead, put on the Lord Jesus Christ like a whole outfit. And don't leave no room for the flesh to act up with its cravings.

14.1: Welcome folks who still tryna grow in their faith—but don't pull up ready to argue over every little opinion.
14.2: Some folks believe they can eat anything, but others—who not as strong yet—stick to vegetables only.
14.3: If you eat, don't look down on the one who don't. And if you don't eat, don't judge the one who do—'cause God already accepted them.
14.4: Who you think you are judgin' somebody else's servant? That's between them and their Master. And trust, they gon' stand—'cause God able to hold them up.
14.5: One person sees some days as more important than others. Another sees every day the same. Let everybody be solid in their own mind.
14.6: If somebody honors a day, they do it for the Lord. If somebody doesn't, they still doin' that for the Lord too. Same thing with food—whether you eat or don't eat, just give God thanks.
14.7: 'Cause ain't none of us livin' just for ourselves—and we ain't dyin' for ourselves either.
14.8: If we live, it's for the Lord. If we die, it's still for the Lord. Either way—we belong to Him.
14.9: Christ died and rose again so He could be Lord over both the livin' and the dead.
14.10: So why you judgin' your brother? Or why you throwin' shade on your sister? We all gon' stand in front of Christ one day.
14.11: Like Scripture says: "As surely as I live," says the Lord, "Every knee gon' bow to Me, And every tongue gon' confess to God."
14.12: So each of us gotta answer for ourselves to God.
14.13: So let's stop judgin' each other. Instead, make sure you ain't blockin' somebody else's walk—don't trip 'em up or slow 'em down.
14.14: I'm convinced—Jesus showed me—nothin' is unclean in itself. But if someone believes it's unclean, then it's unclean for them.
14.15: If your food messin' with your brother's heart, then you not walkin' in love no more. Don't ruin somebody Jesus died for over what's on your plate.
14.16: Don't let your freedom get talked about like it's evil.
14.17: 'Cause the Kingdom of God ain't about what you eat or drink—it's about righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
14.18: If you livin' like that? You servin' Christ right, and God and people gon' respect that.
14.19: So let's chase after what brings peace and builds people up.
14.20: Don't tear down what God built just 'cause of some food. Everything might be clean, but it's still wrong if eatin' it trips somebody else up.
14.21: It's better not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything that'll cause your brother or sister to stumble or feel weak.
14.22: Got strong faith? Cool. Keep that between you and God. Blessed is the one who don't feel guilty for what they approve.
14.23: But if somebody doubts and still eats? That's sin for them—'cause they ain't eatin' from faith. And whatever's not from faith… is sin.

15.1: So look—those of us who strong in faith gotta be patient with those who ain't there yet. Don't just please yourself.
15.2: Each of us should try to please our neighbor, doin' good to build them up.
15.3: Even Jesus didn't live to please Himself. Like Scripture say: "The insults people threw at You fell on Me."
15.4: The stuff written in the past was written to teach us. It's supposed to give us patience and comfort through the Scriptures, so we can have hope.
15.5: Now, may the God of patience and comfort give you the same mind, the same heart toward each other, just like Christ Jesus had.
15.6: That way, we all speak the same thing, glorifyin' God with one mind and one voice—our Father, the Lord Jesus Christ.
15.7: So, accept each other just like Christ accepted you—for God's glory.
15.8: Now check this—Jesus came to serve the Jews, to make sure God's promises to the ancestors stay solid.
15.9: And so that the Gentiles could praise God for His mercy, like it's written: "Because of this, I'm gon' praise You among the Gentiles, And sing to Your name."
15.10: Again it's written: "Rejoice, Gentiles, with His people!"
15.11: Again: "Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, And lift Him up, all you nations!"
15.12: And Isaiah said: "There gon' be a root from Jesse, And He gon' rise to rule over the Gentiles, And the Gentiles gon' put their hope in Him."
15.13: So may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe, so that you overflow with hope, all by the power of the Holy Spirit.
15.14: Now, I'm confident about y'all, my people—you full of goodness, full of knowledge, and ready to teach each other.
15.15: But I've been a little bold with some of this stuff, remindin' you, 'cause of the grace God gave me.
15.16: God set me up to be a minister of Jesus Christ to the Gentiles, spreadin' the gospel so that the Gentiles can be accepted, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
15.17: So yeah, I got reason to be proud in Christ—about the work I've done for God.
15.18: I ain't gon' talk about nothin' Christ didn't do through me, though, in word or deed, to make the Gentiles obey.
15.19: Through signs, wonders, and the power of the Holy Spirit, I've covered a lot of ground—from Jerusalem all the way to Illyricum. I've fully preached the gospel.
15.20: My goal has been to preach the gospel where nobody's preached before—so I won't be buildin' on somebody else's foundation.
15.21: Like it's written: "To folks who ain't heard, they gon' see; And the ones who never heard, they gon' understand."
15.22: That's why I been blocked from comin' to y'all.
15.23: But now, I ain't got no more places left to work in these parts, and I've been tryna come to y'all for years.
15.24: When I head to Spain, I'm gon' stop by y'all. I hope to see you while I'm on my way, and I'm countin' on you to help me get there after I hang with you for a bit.
15.25: But first, I'm headin' to Jerusalem to serve the saints.
15.26: The folks from Macedonia and Achaia decided to help out by sendin' a contribution for the poor saints in Jerusalem.
15.27: It was their honor to give, 'cause if the Gentiles shared in their spiritual blessings, it's only right they share in the material blessings too.
15.28: So when I finish this and seal it with them, I'll be on my way to see y'all, headin' to Spain.
15.29: And I know when I get to you, it's gon' be with the full blessing of the gospel of Christ.
15.30: So, I'm beggin' y'all, fam, through the Lord Jesus Christ and the love of the Spirit, to strive with me in prayer to God for me—
15.31: That I be delivered from the unbelievers in Judea, and that the service I'm doin' in Jerusalem be accepted by the saints.
15.32: So that I can come to y'all with joy, by God's will, and be refreshed by your company.
15.33: Now, may the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

16.1: I'm shoutin' out Phoebe, our sister in Christ. She a real one—servin' with the church in Cenchrea.
16.2: Show her love and welcome her like family. Help her out with anything she need—she been a blessing to many, includin' me.
16.3: Give love to Priscilla and Aquila—my folks who ride for Jesus and for me.
16.4: They risked their lives for me. I'm thankful—and so are all the Gentile churches.
16.5: Show love to the church that meets in their house too. Give a big shoutout to my dude Epaenetus—the first to get saved out in Achaia.
16.6: Greet Mary—sis went hard for the crew.
16.7: Andronicus and Junia? Salute them. They fam and did time with me. Folks respect them as apostles. They was reppin' Christ before I even was.
16.8: Say what's up to Amplias—my guy in the Lord.
16.9: Urbanus, another one of our co-laborers, and Stachys—much love.
16.10: Show love to Apelles—he passed the test in Christ. Say hey to the crew in Aristobulus's house.
16.11: Herodion—what up fam. And the folks from Narcissus's house who follow the Lord.
16.12: Tryphena and Tryphosa—faithful women in the Lord. And Persis? She be goin' in for the Kingdom.
16.13: Greet Rufus, chosen by God, and his mama—she like a mother to me too.
16.14: Say what's up to Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the whole crew with them.
16.15: Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, Olympas—love to all y'all saints.
16.16: Y'all greet each other with a holy hug or kiss—whatever's holy. The churches of Christ all send their love too.
16.17: I gotta keep it real—watch out for folks who stir up division and go against what you been taught. Stay away from them.
16.18: They not servin' Jesus—they servin' themselves. Real slick with their words, flatterin' folks and leadin' the simple-minded astray.
16.19: People already heard about how obedient y'all are—and I'm proud. But I still want you to be wise when it comes to good… and innocent when it comes to evil.
16.20: And best believe—God, the God of peace, gon' crush Satan under your feet real soon. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with y'all. Amen.
16.21: Timothy—my ride-or-die ministry partner—sends love. So do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater—my kinfolk.
16.22: I'm Tertius—the one who actually wrote this down for Paul—and I'm sendin' y'all love too, in the Lord.
16.23: Gaius, who's hostin' me and the whole church, sends his love. Erastus, the city treasurer, and Quartus, our brother, say hey.
16.24: The grace of Jesus be with all of y'all. Amen.
16.25: Now to the One who can hold you down and keep you strong by the gospel I preach—Jesus Christ. The mystery that been hidden since forever,
16.26: but now made known through the Scriptures to all nations, just like God commanded—so folks can walk in real faith and obedience—
16.27: To God, the only wise One—all glory through Jesus Christ, forever and ever. Amen.
